item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00243","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C25","C16","C18"],"selected_candidate_label":"C25","confidence":0.93,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C25 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. It presents the same distinctive policy framework: preserving an adequate merchant fleet for national defense and international commerce while preventing excessive Federal assistance; it specifically groups tax benefits with construction subsidies, operating subsidies, and other privileges; and it directs an executive official to investigate corrective action and recommend new legislation if existing law is inadequate. The child adapts that framework into a broader Commerce Department study of eliminating maritime tax benefits, reassessing all Federal aid, and recommending the necessary amount and form of direct subsidy. C16 shares the merchant-ship construction and subsidy context but not the child's critical reassessment of excessive assistance. C18 has a parallel study-assignment structure but concerns a different substantive policy problem.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"the tax benefits now enjoyed by the shipping industry are excessive in amount","parent_excerpt":"the amount of subsidy involved in the contract sales price for the ship has been seriously challenged as being excessive","explanation":"Both identify excessive Federal benefits to the shipping industry as the problem requiring executive correction."},{"child_excerpt":"maintaining an adequate maritime fleet for our national defense and foreign trade","parent_excerpt":"the maintenance of a strong and healthy American flag merchant fleet...for reasons of national defense and our international commerce","explanation":"This is a close and distinctive statement of the same dual justification for maritime assistance."},{"child_excerpt":"tax benefits represent only one of the many forms of assistance now provided to the shipping industry","parent_excerpt":"construction subsidies, operating subsidies, tax benefits, and other privileges accorded by the Merchant Marine Act","explanation":"C25 supplies the same concrete classification of tax benefits as one component of a larger Federal maritime-assistance system."},{"child_excerpt":"If changes in present Federal policies are needed...please include appropriate recommendations...Should you conclude...that some increase in direct subsidy would be required...I would wish to receive your recommendations","parent_excerpt":"determine what legal action should be taken by the Government...In the event you should find it impossible to take corrective action under existing law, please consider the kind of new legislation that could be recommended","explanation":"Both use an agency-directed review followed by recommendations for corrective administrative or legislative action."}]}
